body: Following the leak of Apple’s App Store frontend source code caused by [source maps](https://github.com/tc39/ecma426) being enabled in production, it may be beneficial to add an explicit requirement advising against enabling source maps in production environments.

comments.body:
Note: I renamed the issue, as it was referencing to non-existing requirement which was misleading.

We have requirements:
| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **13.4.1** | Verify that the application is deployed either without any source control metadata, including the .git or .svn folders, or in a way that these folders are inaccessible both externally and to the application itself. | 1 |
| **13.4.2** | Verify that debug modes are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features and information leakage. | 2 |

I would say that the principle is covered by those and proposed requirement is just a technology-specific test-case.

Pardon my misleading title.

I agree, however, isn't (for example), 1.3.8, already covered by 1.2.6, and 1.3.8 is just a technology-specific test-case?

| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| 1.3.8 | Verify that the application appropriately sanitizes untrusted input before use in Java Naming and Directory Interface (JNDI) queries and that JNDI is configured securely to prevent JNDI injection attacks. | 2 |
| 1.2.6 | Verify that the application protects against LDAP injection vulnerabilities, or that specific security controls to prevent LDAP injection have been implemented. | 2 |

By principle, we can say that the entire "encoding" section is one requirement: Verify that the encoding is chosen based on the syntax rules.

We need to look for the balance between niche and clear and actionable requirements to address widespread problems with a special spotlight. And by nature, it is a good fuel for "whataboutism".

Revisiting the list of requirements - maybe the 13.4.7 is an even more accurate requirement to address the concern:
| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **13.4.7** | Verify that the web tier is configured to only serve files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information, configuration, and source code leakage. | 3 |

I am surprised source maps have never been mentioned before. 

I think 13.4.7 is talking about something slightly different, I would be more included to include this in one of these:

| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **13.4.2** | Verify that debug modes are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features and information leakage. | 2 |
| **13.4.5** | Verify that documentation (such as for internal APIs) and monitoring endpoints are not exposed unless explicitly intended. | 2 |

What do we think?

@tghosth I concur regarding 13.4.7. 

I do believe that source maps deserve a standalone requirement, because, although they aid in debugging, they are not "debug modes" per se.

However, I vouch for 13.4.2:

| # | Description | Level
| -- | -- | -- |
| 13.4.2 | Verify that debug modes, are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features, such as source maps, and information leakage. | 2 |

Or:

| # | Description | Level
| -- | -- | -- |
| 13.4.2 | Verify that debug modes, such as source maps, are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features and information leakage. | 2 |
Ok so I am going to leave this open for now as it requires us finalising our change control mechanism

title: proposal 13.4.* Verify that source maps are disabled in production environments to prevent source code leakage.
